merge.q: How do I merge PDF files?
merge.a: Simply drag and drop your PDF files into the upload area, reorder them as needed, and click "Merge & Download". The combined PDF will be downloaded instantly.

merge.q: Is there a limit on the number of files?
merge.a: No, you can merge as many PDF files as your browser can handle. There is no artificial limit on file count or size.

merge.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
merge.a: No. All processing happens 100% in your browser. Your files never leave your device — we have zero access to your documents.

merge.q: Can I reorder pages before merging?
merge.a: Yes! After uploading your files, you can drag and drop them into any order before merging.
No. The merge process preserves the original quality of every page in your PDFs. No compression or modification is applied.

merge.q: Do I need to sign up?
merge.a: No. MergesPDF is completely free with no sign-up, no login, and no email required. Just upload and merge.

split.a: Upload a PDF file and choose to split all pages into individual files, or enter a page range (e.g., "1-3, 5") to extract specific pages into a new PDF.
Yes! Switch to "Page Range" mode and enter the pages you want, like "1-3, 5, 8-10". They'll be combined into a single new PDF.
No. You can split PDFs of any size — there are no artificial page or file size limits.

split.q: Are the split files the same quality?
split.a: Yes. Pages are copied without any re-encoding, so quality is preserved exactly as the original.
Completely free. No subscriptions, no watermarks, no hidden costs.

compress.a: Our compressor strips unnecessary metadata, rebuilds the document structure, and removes unused objects to reduce file size without affecting visible content.
The compression technique we use focuses on metadata removal and structure optimization. The visible content and page quality remain unchanged.

compress.q: How much can I reduce the file size?
compress.a: Results vary by document. PDFs with lots of metadata, unused fonts, or duplicated objects can see 10-60% size reduction.

compress.q: Is there a file size limit?
compress.a: There is no hard limit, but very large files (100MB+) may be slower to process since everything runs in your browser.

compress.q: Can I compress multiple PDFs at once?
compress.a: Yes! Use the Batch Processing tool to compress multiple PDFs simultaneously with progress tracking.

rotate.q: How do I rotate PDF pages?
rotate.a: Upload a PDF, select the rotation angle (90°, 180°, or 270°), and click Rotate. The rotated PDF will download instantly.

rotate.q: Can I rotate specific pages only?
rotate.a: Currently, rotation applies to all pages in the PDF. For selective page rotation, split the PDF first, rotate individual pages, then merge them back.
No, rotation only changes the page orientation. All text, images, and formatting remain exactly the same.
Yes — simply rotate the PDF again. For example, if you rotated 90° clockwise, rotate 270° to return to the original orientation.

encrypt.a: Enter a password and we rebuild the PDF with protection metadata. For maximum security, use a desktop tool like Adobe Acrobat with the password you set here.

encrypt.q: Can I remove the password later?
encrypt.a: You can re-open the protected PDF with your password in any PDF reader. To remove the password, open it in a PDF editor and save without protection.
Browser-based encryption has limitations compared to desktop tools. For highly sensitive documents, we recommend using the password with a professional PDF encryption tool.
Yes, anyone who wants to open the encrypted PDF will need the password you set.

pdfToWord.q: How does PDF to Word conversion work?
pdfToWord.a: We extract the document structure from your PDF and create a Word (.docx) file. The conversion preserves page structure and basic formatting.
Browser-based conversion has limitations. For complex PDFs with embedded fonts or advanced layouts, a desktop tool may produce better results.
The output is a Microsoft Word .docx file that can be opened in Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice, and most word processors.
No. Everything is processed in your browser. Your file never leaves your device.

wordToPdf.a: We support .doc and .docx files. For best results, use .docx format.
The converter extracts text content and renders it into a well-formatted PDF. Complex formatting may not be fully preserved.

wordToPdf.q: What about images in the Word file?
wordToPdf.a: Currently, text content is extracted and converted. Embedded images in Word documents may not appear in the output PDF.

wordToPdf.q: Is there a file size limit?
wordToPdf.a: No hard limit, but very large documents may take longer to process since everything runs in your browser.

deletePages.q: How do I delete pages from a PDF?
deletePages.a: Upload a PDF, enter the page numbers you want to remove (e.g., "1-3, 5"), and click Delete Pages. A new PDF without those pages will be downloaded.
The original file is never modified. If you need the deleted pages back, simply use the original file again.

deletePages.q: Can I delete all pages except one?
deletePages.a: Yes, but you must keep at least one page. Enter all pages except the one you want to keep.
Yes. The remaining pages keep their original order after deletion.

extractPages.q: How do I extract pages from a PDF?
extractPages.a: Upload a PDF, enter the page numbers you want (e.g., "1-3, 5, 8"), and click Extract. A new PDF with only those pages will be downloaded.

extractPages.q: What's the difference between Extract and Split?
extractPages.a: Extract combines selected pages into one new PDF. Split creates individual files for each page.

extractPages.q: Can I extract pages in a different order?
extractPages.a: Pages are extracted in the order they appear in the original document.
Yes. Pages are copied without any re-encoding, preserving the original quality exactly.

watermark.q: What kind of watermarks can I add?
watermark.a: You can add text watermarks with customizable font size, opacity, and rotation. The watermark is applied diagonally across every page.

watermark.q: Can I add an image watermark?
watermark.a: Currently only text watermarks are supported. Image watermark support is coming soon.

watermark.q: Can I control the watermark position?
watermark.a: The watermark is centered and rotated at 45° for maximum coverage. You can adjust opacity and font size.
The watermark is embedded directly into the PDF. It cannot be easily removed, making it effective for document protection.

flatten.q: What does flattening a PDF do?
flatten.a: Flattening removes form fields, annotations, layers, and interactive elements, producing a static, non-editable PDF.
Yes, completely free with no limits or sign-up required.
It can. By removing interactive elements and rebuilding the structure, the file often becomes smaller.

grayscale.q: What does converting to grayscale do?
grayscale.a: It rebuilds your PDF without color data, resulting in a black-and-white document that is often smaller in file size.

grayscale.q: Will this reduce my file size?
grayscale.a: In many cases yes, especially for PDFs with color images or graphics.
No. Color information is removed permanently. Keep the original file if you may need color again.

pageNumbers.q: How do I add page numbers to a PDF?
pageNumbers.a: Upload your PDF, choose top or bottom position, then click "Add Page Numbers". The tool adds sequential numbers to every page.
Yes, completely free with no limits, no watermarks, and no account required.
You can choose between top-center and bottom-center placement.

unlock.q: What restrictions can this tool remove?
unlock.a: It removes print, copy, and edit restrictions (owner password). It cannot bypass open-password protection.
Yes, completely free. No sign-up or limits.
Removing restrictions from PDFs you own or have permission to modify is legal. Do not use this tool on documents you don't have the right to unlock.

batch.a: You can batch merge (combine all PDFs into one) or batch compress (compress each PDF individually) with progress tracking.

batch.q: How many files can I process at once?
batch.a: There is no artificial limit. Process as many files as your browser can handle.
Yes! A progress bar shows the status of each file being processed.
Yes. All batch processing happens in your browser. No files are uploaded to any server.

formFiller.q: How does the PDF form filler work?
formFiller.a: Upload a PDF with form fields, and the tool automatically detects all fillable fields. Enter your values and download the completed PDF.

formFiller.q: What types of form fields are supported?
formFiller.a: Text fields are fully supported. The tool detects all PDF form field types including text inputs, checkboxes, and dropdowns.

formFiller.q: Will the form data be embedded in the PDF?
formFiller.a: Yes — the form is flattened after filling, so the data becomes part of the PDF content.

formFiller.q: What if my PDF has no form fields?
formFiller.a: The tool will let you know if no fillable fields are detected. Only PDFs with interactive form fields will work.

redact.a: Upload a PDF and draw black rectangles over sensitive areas on each page. The redacted PDF will have those areas permanently blacked out.
Yes — black rectangles are drawn directly onto the PDF content. The original text underneath is covered.
No. Once saved, the redaction is permanent. Always keep a copy of the original file.
Yes. Your PDF never leaves your device. All redaction happens in your browser.

pdfToImages.q: How do I convert PDF to images?
pdfToImages.a: Upload a PDF, select the image format (PNG or JPG) and quality, then click Convert. Each page becomes a separate image.
1x for standard resolution, 2x for high quality (recommended), and 3x for maximum detail.
Currently, all pages are converted. You can use our Split tool first to extract specific pages.
Yes, especially at 2x or 3x quality. The images are rendered at the PDF's native resolution multiplied by your chosen scale.

mergeImages.q: What image formats can I merge into a PDF?
mergeImages.a: You can combine JPG, JPEG, PNG, and WEBP images into a single PDF document.

mergeImages.q: Can I reorder the images before merging?
mergeImages.a: Yes! Simply drag and drop the image thumbnails to arrange them in your preferred order.

mergeImages.q: Is there a limit on the number of images?
mergeImages.a: No artificial limit. Add as many images as your browser can handle.
Images are embedded at their original resolution. No compression or quality loss is applied.

ocr.a: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) converts images of text into machine-readable text, making scanned documents searchable and editable.
English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), Hindi, and Japanese.
Yes! Tesseract.js runs entirely in your browser. Your files never leave your device.
Processing time depends on page count and complexity. Most single-page documents complete in under 10 seconds.

ocr.q: Can I OCR a scanned PDF?
ocr.a: Yes! Upload a scanned PDF and the tool will render each page, then extract text using OCR.

editor.q: What can I do with the PDF Editor?
editor.a: Add text, highlights, freehand drawings, lines, arrows, rectangles, circles, sticky notes, and images to any PDF page.
Yes! All rendering and editing happens in your browser. Your PDF never leaves your device.
Yes — use Ctrl+Z to undo and Ctrl+Y to redo. The editor maintains a full undo/redo history.

editor.q: Will my annotations be part of the PDF?
editor.a: Yes. When you save, all annotations are permanently embedded into the PDF.

editor.q: Can I edit text already in the PDF?
editor.a: The editor focuses on adding annotations. To edit existing text, you may need a desktop tool.

svgToImage.q: What image formats can I convert SVG to?
svgToImage.a: You can convert to PNG, JPG, WEBP, and BMP — all processed in your browser.
SVGs are vector-based so they scale perfectly. Choose a higher scale (2x–4x) for crisp output.

svgToImage.q: Is my SVG uploaded to a server?
svgToImage.a: No. Everything runs 100% in your browser. Your files never leave your device.

svgToImage.q: Can I convert SVGs with transparency?
svgToImage.a: Yes! PNG and WEBP preserve transparency. JPG and BMP will have a white background.

excelToPdf.a: You can convert .xlsx, .xls, and .csv files to PDF.

excelToPdf.q: Are my spreadsheets uploaded to a server?
excelToPdf.a: No. All processing happens 100% in your browser. Your files never leave your device.
The converter renders table data with gridlines and headers. Complex Excel formatting like charts may not be preserved.

excelToPdf.q: Is there a file size limit?
excelToPdf.a: No artificial limit — it depends on your browser's memory capacity.

pptxToPdf.a: Currently .pptx files are supported. Older .ppt files need to be saved as .pptx first.

pptxToPdf.q: Are my presentations uploaded to a server?
pptxToPdf.a: No. Everything is processed 100% in your browser. Your files never leave your device.

pptxToPdf.q: Does it preserve images and animations?
pptxToPdf.a: The converter extracts text content and layout. Complex animations and embedded media may not be fully rendered.

pptxToPdf.q: Do I need to sign up?
pptxToPdf.a: No. This tool is completely free with no sign-up required.

webpageToPdf.q: How do I convert HTML to PDF?
webpageToPdf.a: Paste your HTML code or upload an HTML file, then click "Convert to PDF". The PDF will be generated instantly.

webpageToPdf.q: Can I convert a live webpage?
webpageToPdf.a: You can save a webpage as HTML (Ctrl+S / Cmd+S) and then upload the file to convert it to PDF.

webpageToPdf.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
webpageToPdf.a: No. All processing happens 100% in your browser. Your data never leaves your device.
The converter extracts structured text content (headings, paragraphs, lists). Complex CSS layouts may be simplified.

heicToPdf.a: HEIC (High Efficiency Image Container) is Apple's default photo format on iPhone and iPad. It offers better compression than JPEG while maintaining quality.

heicToPdf.q: What can I convert HEIC to?
heicToPdf.a: You can convert HEIC/HEIF images to JPG, PNG, or combine them into a single PDF document.

heicToPdf.q: Are my photos uploaded to a server?
heicToPdf.a: No. All conversion happens 100% in your browser. Your photos never leave your device.

heicToPdf.q: Can I convert multiple HEIC files at once?
heicToPdf.a: Yes! You can select multiple HEIC/HEIF files and convert them all at once.

repairPdf.q: What types of PDF damage can be repaired?
repairPdf.a: This tool can fix corrupted cross-reference tables, broken page trees, damaged metadata, and re-index pages for a clean structure.

repairPdf.q: Will repairing change my PDF content?
repairPdf.a: No. The repair process preserves all existing page content. It only fixes the internal structure and metadata.

repairPdf.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
repairPdf.a: No. All repair processing happens 100% in your browser. Your files never leave your device.

repairPdf.q: What if my PDF is too damaged to repair?
repairPdf.a: Severely corrupted files (e.g., truncated or encrypted with unknown passwords) may not be recoverable. The tool will let you know.

pdfBookmarks.a: PDF bookmarks are a table of contents that appears as a sidebar in PDF readers, allowing quick navigation to specific sections or pages.
Yes! You can add as many bookmarks as you need, each pointing to a different page in your PDF document.

pdfBookmarks.q: Will this modify my PDF content?
pdfBookmarks.a: No. Adding bookmarks only adds navigation metadata — your actual page content remains completely unchanged.

pdfBookmarks.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
pdfBookmarks.a: No. All processing happens 100% in your browser. Your files never leave your device.

pageSize.a: We support A4, A3, A5, Letter, Legal, Tabloid, B5, and Executive sizes. Content is automatically scaled and centered.
No. Content is proportionally scaled to fit the new page size while maintaining its aspect ratio, then centered on the page.
Currently, the tool resizes all pages to the same target size. For individual page sizing, use the Crop tool.

pageSize.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
pageSize.a: No. All processing happens 100% in your browser. Your files never leave your device.

pdfToExcel.q: How does PDF to Excel extraction work?
pdfToExcel.a: The tool reads each page of your PDF, groups text by position into rows and columns, and exports the structured data as an Excel spreadsheet or CSV file.

pdfToExcel.q: Will it work with scanned PDFs?
pdfToExcel.a: This tool extracts text-based content. For scanned/image PDFs, use the OCR tool first to make text extractable, then convert to Excel.
You can download the extracted data as an .xlsx (Excel) file or a .csv file for maximum compatibility.

pdfToExcel.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
pdfToExcel.a: No. All processing happens 100% in your browser. Your files never leave your device.

epubToPdf.a: EPUB is a popular e-book format used by most e-readers (except Kindle). This tool converts EPUB files to PDF while preserving chapters and reading order.

epubToPdf.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
epubToPdf.a: No. All processing happens 100% in your browser. Your files never leave your device.

epubToPdf.q: Will images from the EPUB be included?
epubToPdf.a: Currently the tool extracts and renders text content. Complex layouts and embedded images may be simplified.

htmlToPdf.q: How do I convert HTML to PDF?
htmlToPdf.a: Paste your HTML code or upload an HTML file, then click "Convert to PDF". The tool renders the structured content into a PDF document.

htmlToPdf.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
htmlToPdf.a: No. All processing happens 100% in your browser.

pdfA.a: PDF/A is an ISO-standardized version of PDF designed for long-term digital preservation of documents. It ensures the document can be reproduced exactly the same way in the future.

pdfA.q: What changes does the conversion make?
pdfA.a: The tool adds required metadata (title, author, dates), embeds fonts, and sets PDF/A identification markers for archival compliance.

pdfA.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
pdfA.a: No. All processing happens 100% in your browser.

scanToPdf.q: Can I use my phone camera?
scanToPdf.a: Yes! On mobile devices, the "Take Photo" button opens your camera directly. You can also upload existing images from your gallery.
JPG and PNG images are supported. Each image becomes one page in the resulting PDF, scaled to fit A4 size.

scanToPdf.q: Are my photos uploaded to a server?
scanToPdf.a: No. All processing happens 100% in your browser. Your photos never leave your device.

pdfOverlay.a: PDF overlay places one PDF on top of another — useful for adding letterheads, stamps, watermarks, or backgrounds to existing documents.

pdfOverlay.q: What is the difference between foreground and background?
pdfOverlay.a: Foreground places the overlay on top of the base PDF. Background places it behind, useful for adding letterhead templates.

pdfOverlay.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
pdfOverlay.a: No. All processing happens 100% in your browser.

comparePdf.a: We extract text from both PDFs page by page and compare them to find differences. The similarity score shows how much text overlaps.
Only if the scanned PDF has a text layer (OCR). Image-only scans cannot be compared for text differences.
No. All comparison happens 100% in your browser. Your files never leave your device.

pdfToPpt.a: The output is an HTML presentation file that can be opened in any browser and printed. Each PDF page becomes one slide.
Currently, text content is extracted from each page. For image-heavy PDFs, consider using PDF to Images instead.
No. All processing happens 100% in your browser.

markdownToPdf.a: Headings (H1-H3), bullet lists, numbered lists, blockquotes, code blocks, horizontal rules, bold, italic, and links are all supported.
Yes! Click "Load .md File" to import a Markdown file, or paste your text directly into the editor.
No. All conversion happens 100% in your browser.
